strategy.summary: The Orders API spec documents GET /products/{id} (getProduct) and POST /orders/{id}/cancel (cancelOrder), but no test calls them. Add Vitest API tests (real app in-process, as the existing specs do) for each one's success response and every error response the spec documents (404 for both, 409 for cancelling an already-cancelled order). Running the suite also showed that the existing GET /orders/{id} test still asserts the old `totalCents` field, while the spec (and the app) now return `total: { amount, currency }`. That test gets updated to the current contract.
inScope: POST /orders/{id}/cancel: 200 Order (status cancelled), 404 Error and 409 Error
Updating the existing GET /orders/{id} success test from totalCents to the spec's total Money object, keeping all its other checks
outOfScope: Operations that tests already call (listProducts, placeOrder), apart from the stale getOrder assertion
Changes to the spec or the application
Restructuring the existing specs (e.g. a shared server helper); listed as a follow-up only
assumptions: The app runs for real, in-process: createApp() listens on port 0 in each spec file, as test/products.test.js and test/orders.test.js already do. Nothing is faked.
Each createApp() gets a fresh in-memory store, so each test creates the order it cancels and asserts only on that order.

The new tests go into the existing spec files beside each resource's tests (getProduct in test/products.test.js, cancelOrder in test/orders.test.js). They reuse those files' server setup instead of copying it.

risks.description: Cancelling puts the stock back, which could change what other tests in the same file see if they depend on stock
risks.mitigation: Cancel tests use product 3 (Mug, stock 40). The stock-short test uses product 4 (stock 0), so neither affects the other.

risks.description: A test could pass without checking the contract if it asserted only the status
risks.mitigation: Each test asserts the status, the JSON content type and the full body shape. Values that the request determines (id, status, total amount and currency) are checked exactly.

acceptanceCriteria.text: GET /products/{id} returns 200 with the Product (id, name, priceCents, stock) for an existing id, and 404 with an Error body for an unknown id

POST /orders/{id}/cancel returns 200 with the Order, status cancelled, for a placed order; 404 with an Error body for an unknown order; and 409 with an Error body for an order that is already cancelled
The tests of GET /orders/{id} assert the current contract: the total is a Money object {amount, currency}

testCases.title: returns one product
testCases.expected: 200, application/json, body equals the Teapot product {id: 2, name, priceCents, stock} from the seed catalogue (store PRODUCTS)
testCases.rationale: getProduct (GET /products/{id}) is untested. This covers its 200 Product response.

testCases.title: is 404 for an unknown product
testCases.rationale: getProduct: covers the spec's documented 404 NotFound response.

testCases.title: cancels a placed order
preconditions: An order placed by the test for product 3, quantity 2
testCases.expected: 200, application/json, body equals {id, productId: 3, quantity: 2, status: 'cancelled', total: {amount: 1398, currency: 'USD'}}
testCases.rationale: cancelOrder (POST /orders/{id}/cancel) is untested. This covers its 200 Order response.

testCases.title: is 404 when cancelling an unknown order
testCases.rationale: cancelOrder: covers the spec's documented 404 response.

testCases.title: is 409 when the order is already cancelled
preconditions: An order placed and cancelled by the test
testCases.rationale: cancelOrder: covers the spec's documented 409 response.

testCases.title: returns an order with its total
preconditions: An order placed by the test for product 1, quantity 2
testCases.expected: 200, body equals {id, productId: 1, quantity: 2, status: 'placed', total: {amount: 4998, currency: 'USD'}}
testCases.rationale: getOrder: the existing test asserts the old totalCents field and fails against the app. The spec's Order.total is now a Money object, so the assertion moves to the new shape and keeps checking the same amount. Its other checks stay as they are.

strategy.environmentNotes: No external services. Each spec starts the app in-process on an OS-chosen port and fetches against it.
